PHRIEND: FULL TEXT FOR AI ASSISTANTS
Source: https://phriend.app (landing features and FAQ), https://phriend.app/safety, https://phriend.app/community-guidelines
Last updated: 2026-10-06. Short version: https://phriend.app/llms.txt

What is Phriend?
Phriend is a Philippine app for booking ID-verified local guides and pros by the hour: city and food tours, photo and video shoots, tutoring and lessons, hiking guides, drivers and errand helpers. Members are 18+, meet in public places, and pay 50% in cash on a first meetup and 50% after. The app runs in the browser at https://web.phriend.app. Contact: support@phriend.app.


==================================================
FEATURES
https://phriend.app/#features
==================================================

Search and favorites: filter by city, gender, language, activity, area, keyword, age and rate, narrow by sub-activity, favorite profiles that follow your account, and share a profile link.

Bookings: pick a service, a date, start time, 1 to 8 hours and a meeting place (a public place, or the client's address for a home service), add a note, and send the request up to 60 days ahead. The Phriend accepts or declines; either side can cancel with a reason and mark the meetup completed afterwards. Add it to Google Calendar or download the .ics. Money never moves in the app: 50% in cash on a first meetup, 50% after; e-wallets only for repeat, trusted Phriends.

Schedule: Phriends set their weekly days and hours and lock out dates up to a year ahead. Requests outside those hours, on a locked-out date or over an accepted booking are refused.

Services and rates: on top of their hourly rate, each Phriend lists up to 12 services, each with its own price per hour or per session, a minimum number of hours and an optional photo.

Chat: photos, emojis, saved replies, typing and online indicators. Delete a message for everyone, archive a chat, block a member. Offensive language is refused: two warnings, then escalating mutes.

Reviews: any signed-in member can review a Phriend: a star rating, a few words and up to 4 photos, one review per member per Phriend. Reviews show on the profile next to the verified badge.

Manage dashboard (Phriends): profile views, favorites, reviews, bookings by status and an earnings estimate (cash, paid in person), plus private notes they can link to a booking and an activity log.

Gigs board: post what you need: the activity, city, budget per hour, date and details. Phriends with a live profile mark interest and chat; anyone can report a gig.

Notifications: a bell in the app and an email for every booking request, acceptance, decline, cancellation and completion, and for every new review.

Safety: ID verification through Didit before a profile goes live. Sample profiles are marked as samples and cannot be booked. Reports, profiles and gigs get an AI first pass; unclear cases go to one of our moderators, and every action is logged.

Teams: a team is a group of ID-verified Phriends who offer a service together, with one team page, one group chat, one price per group and one booking. Each member keeps their own profile and can still be booked alone. Browse teams by city at https://phriend.app/teams.

Your account: sign in with Google, or with your email and a password (confirmed by a 6-digit code). Delete your account yourself by typing DELETE; your profile, photos, favorites, reviews, bookings, notes and gigs go with it.

Cash, in person: money never moves in the app. Pay a 50% downpayment and 50% after. On a first meetup the downpayment is cash in person; e-wallets are for repeat Phriends you already trust. Never more than half upfront.


==================================================
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
==================================================

Q: What can I book on Phriend?
A: Local services and activities, by the hour: guided city and food tours, photo and video shoots, tutoring and lessons, hiking and trail guiding, personal training, driving and airport transfers, errands and queueing, event coverage and on-site help. Phriend is not a dating service. Romantic or sexual services, compensated dating and escort services are banned and get an account removed immediately.

Q: How do bookings work?
A: Send the Phriend a booking request with the date, start time, number of hours (1 to 8), a meeting place (a public place, or the client's address for a home service) and a note, up to 60 days ahead. If the Phriend lists services, pick one; some need a minimum number of hours. The Phriend accepts or declines, either side can cancel with a reason, and once the meetup time has passed either side can mark it completed. Every booking has an Add to Google Calendar button and an .ics download. Money never moves in the app: 50% in cash when you meet, 50% after.

Q: How do I pay?
A: Directly between members, never through Phriend. On a first meetup, hand over 50% in cash, in person, when you meet, then pay the remaining 50% after. GCash, Maya or bank transfer are for repeat Phriends you have already met and trust, for convenience, and only to the account the Phriend shared in the chat. Never pay more than half upfront, and never to an account that is not the one shared in the chat.

Q: What if my Phriend brings someone else?
A: Do not proceed. If the other member arrives with people who were not agreed in the chat, be prudent: cancel the meetup, leave, and report the profile. The same applies to a client who shows up with extra people. On a team booking, the teammates named on the booking are the agreed people; anyone else still is not. A cancellation for this reason is refunded in full.

Q: What is a team?
A: A group of ID-verified Phriends who offer a service together, for example a guide, a photographer and a driver for one day out. A team has one page, packages with a group price and a fixed length, and one group chat. You send one booking request and the team lead accepts or declines for everyone. Every member can also be booked alone. The downpayment is at most 50%, in cash, in person, handed to the team lead, who splits it with the team; Phriend never holds money. If a member cannot make it, the lead cancels or rebooks. Teams are listed at https://phriend.app/teams.

Q: Does Phriend take a commission?
A: Not yet. Members agree on a rate per hour, typically between ₱300 and ₱1,500 depending on the activity and the city, and keep all of it. If this changes we will announce it well ahead of time.

Q: Can I set my own rates and services?
A: Yes. Set your hourly rate (up to ₱3,000) and list up to 12 services, each with its own price per hour or per session (₱50 to ₱50,000), a minimum of 1 to 12 hours if you want one, and an optional photo. You also set your weekly availability and lock out the dates you are busy, so clients can only book when you are free. Phriend takes no cut, so what you list is what you keep.

Q: How does verification work?
A: Members submit a government ID (PhilID, passport, driver's license or UMID) and a selfie through Didit, our identity verification partner. It takes about two minutes. Didit checks the ID and confirms the member is 18 or older; Phriend emails the result and shows the verified badge on their profile. Verification is required before a Phriend profile goes live. Phriend is strictly 18+.

Q: What do Phriends agree to?
A: Before a profile goes live, every Phriend ticks a seven-point agreement: they are 18 or older and will verify with a government ID; they offer legitimate activities only, nothing romantic, sexual or illegal; they meet in public places and never bring or allow anyone not agreed in the chat; payment is 50% at the start and 50% after, cash in person on a first meetup and e-wallets only for repeat clients they trust; they stop the meetup and report it if a client brings extra people not agreed in chat, is very late or makes them uncomfortable; Phriend is a platform only and not liable for what happens between members; and they have read the Terms, Privacy Policy and Community Guidelines.

Q: What are non-negotiables?
A: Rules a Phriend pins to the top of their profile so clients agree before they chat. They pick from: public meet-up only, no physical contact, cash downpayment on arrival, daytime only, no alcohol, no smoking, groups must be agreed in chat, no riding in client vehicles, ID check on arrival, and no overnight or out-of-town.

Q: What are gigs?
A: A gig is a request a client posts: what they need, the activity, city, budget per hour, date and details. Only members with a live Phriend profile can mark interest and chat about it. Anyone can report a gig, and you can delete the gigs you posted.

Q: What if my Phriend is late or cancels?
A: You may cancel if the other member is more than 30 minutes late without notice, and a late Phriend refunds any downpayment already paid in full. Cancellations should happen at least 24 hours before the meetup. The full rules are on the safety page.

Q: Do I need to install anything?
A: No. Phriend runs in the browser at web.phriend.app on any phone. Add it to your home screen and it works like an app, with chat, bookings and in-app notifications.

Q: How do I delete my account?
A: Open My profile, tap Delete account and type DELETE. It permanently removes your account, Phriend profile, photos, favorites, reviews, bookings, notes and gigs. It cannot be undone.


==================================================
SAFETY AND TRANSACTION RULES
https://phriend.app/safety
==================================================

These rules apply to every member, on both sides of a meetup. They are short on purpose. Breaking them gets an account removed. Phriend is a platform only: it is not a party to any meetup or payment and is not liable for any loss, injury, dispute, unpaid balance or harm between members. You use the service at your own risk, and your prudence is your protection.

In short: Meet in public, or at your own home for a home service. Only the people agreed in the chat come along (on a team booking, the teammates named on the booking); if extra people not agreed in chat show up, cancel, leave and report. On a first meetup pay half in cash when you meet and half after, never more than half upfront. E-wallets are for repeat Phriends you trust, and only to the account shared in the chat. Tell a friend where you are, and report anything that feels wrong.

1. Public places, or your home for a home service
Most meetups happen in a public place: a mall, a cafe, a restaurant, a park, a trail, a gym, a hospital lobby, a venue. A home service can happen at the client's home, the client's choice. Never a hotel room, an overnight stay, the Phriend's own place, or a private vehicle you do not both trust. If a member asks to move somewhere private, decline and report them.
For out-of-town trips, hikes and beach days, agree on the meeting point and the route in the chat before the day, and keep the group in public spaces throughout.

2. Extra people not agreed in chat
Who is coming is agreed in the chat, like everything else. If the other member arrives with people who were not agreed in the chat, a friend, a "cousin", a driver who stays, be prudent: do not proceed. Cancel the meetup, leave, and report the profile. This applies to both sides; a client who shows up with extra people is treated the same way.
On a team booking, the teammates named on the booking are the agreed people. Anyone else still is not.
A cancellation for this reason counts as a safety concern under section 9: any downpayment already paid is refunded in full.

3. Payments: 50% at the start, 50% after
- Agree on the rate and the number of hours in the chat and in the booking request, so both sides have a record.
- The client pays 50% at the start of the meetup and the remaining 50% after it ends.
- First meetup: the 50% downpayment is handed over in cash, in person, when the members meet. Nothing is transferred before you have met.
- E-wallets (GCash, Maya) or bank transfer are for repeat Phriends the client has already met and trusts, for convenience. Even then, never more than 50% upfront, and only to the account shared in the chat.
- Never pay more than 50% upfront. No member may ask for full payment, a "reservation fee" on top of the downpayment, or any other advance. A member who pushes for a transfer before a first meetup is a red flag: be prudent and report them.
- The downpayment is deducted from the total. It is not an extra charge.
- Phriend does not process payments and does not hold money. Payments happen directly between members.
- On a team booking, the downpayment is handed to the team lead, who splits it with the team. The same limit applies: never more than 50%.

4. Pay only the account shared in the chat
When a transfer is appropriate, that is with a repeat Phriend you trust, the Phriend shares their GCash, Maya or bank account in the chat. Send money only to that account. Any request to pay a different number, a relative's account, a "company" account, a link, a QR code sent by SMS or Messenger, or anything outside the chat is a scam. Stop, do not pay, and report the member.

5. Tell someone your plan
Before you go, share the meetup place, the time, the other member's profile and your expected return with a friend or family member. Keep your phone charged and your location sharing on. Trust your instincts: if something feels off, leave.

6. Identity verification
Members verify their identity and age through Didit, an independent identity verification provider. Didit checks a government ID and a selfie and confirms the member is 18 or older. Verified profiles show a blue badge. Prefer verified members, and verify yourself so others can trust you.

7. Report and block
Every profile and every gig has a report button, and the chat menu leads to it. Use it for anything that breaks these rules or the community guidelines: requests for private meetups, extra people not agreed in chat, romantic or sexual propositions, off-platform payment requests, harassment, impersonation, or a member who looks under 18. You can attach up to 4 photos as evidence. Blocking, from the chat menu, hides the member's profile and chats and stops their messages reaching you. Reports get an AI first pass; anything unclear goes to one of our moderators, and serious cases are passed to the authorities.

8. Late arrivals
- If a member is more than 30 minutes late without notice, the other member may cancel the meetup.
- If the Phriend is the one late, any downpayment already paid is refunded in full.
- If the client is the one late and the Phriend waited, the agreed hours still count from the agreed start time.

9. Cancellations
- Cancel at least 24 hours before the meetup: cancel the booking in the app with a reason, and say so in the chat.
- If the client cancels with less than 24 hours' notice, the Phriend may keep any downpayment already paid.
- If the Phriend cancels with less than 24 hours' notice, any downpayment already paid is refunded in full. Repeated late cancellations lead to removal.
- Cancellations because of typhoons, floods, extra people not agreed in chat or any other safety concern are refunded in full, no questions asked.

10. Emergencies
If you are in danger, call for help first and report to Phriend later.
- 911: national emergency hotline, connects to the Philippine National Police.
- PNP hotline: 911, or text 0998 598 8888.
- Contact your nearest police station or barangay hall for local assistance.
After you are safe, report the member in the app and email support@phriend.app with the profile name and what happened. We cooperate with law enforcement.

11. The short version
1. Meet in public, or at your own home for a home service.
2. Only the people agreed in the chat (on a team booking, the teammates named on it). Extra people not agreed in chat: cancel, leave, report.
3. First meetup: half in cash when you meet, half after. Never more than half.
4. E-wallet only for repeat Phriends you trust, and only to the account shared in the chat.
5. Tell a friend where you are.
6. Report anything that feels wrong.


==================================================
COMMUNITY GUIDELINES
https://phriend.app/community-guidelines
==================================================

Phriend is for legitimate local services: work and activities you book by the hour, done in public or at the client's home, between adults. This page says exactly what that means.

In short: Phriend is for legitimate local services and activities booked by the hour between adults, in public places or at the client's home for home services: guided tours, photo and video shoots, tutoring and lessons, hiking, driving, errands and the like. Any sexual or romantic service, compensated dating, escort services, drugs, private-place meetups, scams and impersonation are banned and get an account removed immediately, with a report to the authorities where the law requires it.

1. What Phriend is for
A Phriend is a local you book and pay by the hour for a service or an activity: a tour, a shoot, a lesson, a hike, a drive, an errand. The relationship is professional and public. If you would not do it in front of your parents or a police officer, it does not belong on Phriend.

2. Allowed activities
- Food tours, market and street-food guiding, cooking lessons
- City tours, local guiding, out-of-town day trips, beach and island trips
- Hiking and trail guiding, camping, personal training, sports coaching
- Photography, videography and content creation work
- Event, wedding and convention coverage, hosting and on-site help
- Driving, riding and airport transfers
- Tutoring, lessons, language practice, consulting and coaching
- Errands, shopping runs, queueing, moving and delivery help
- Hospital and clinic assistance, elderly care help, waiting-room assistance
- Dog walking and pet sitting
- Online sessions such as tutoring or language practice over video call
If your idea is not on the list but is a legal, professional service done in public or at the client's home, it is probably fine. When in doubt, email support@phriend.app before posting.

3. Prohibited
The following are banned. Offering, requesting or hinting at any of them gets an account removed.
- Any sexual or romantic service. This includes anything "intimate", "private", "special", cuddling, massage, or any physical contact beyond a normal greeting.
- Compensated dating. Phriend is not a dating service. Any arrangement where romance, affection or intimacy is exchanged for money, gifts or favours is banned.
- Escort services of any kind, including "overnight" bookings, trips with shared rooms, or hotel meetups.
- Drugs: buying, selling, using or being under the influence during a meetup.
- Alcohol with minors. Phriend is 18+, and any listing built around drinking that targets or involves anyone under 18 is banned. Drinking is never the point of a booking, and a member who is drunk may be asked to leave.
- Anything illegal under Philippine law, including gambling arrangements, smuggling, fraud and human trafficking.
- Harassment: unwanted contact, threats, stalking, hate speech, or sharing someone's private information.
- Impersonation: using someone else's photos, name or ID, or pretending to be a company or a Phriend staff member.
- Off-platform payment scams: asking for more than 50% upfront, asking for payment to an account not shared in the chat, sending payment links or QR codes outside the app, or requesting gift cards and crypto.
- Meetups in hotel rooms, overnight stays or the Phriend's own place, and home visits for anything that is not a home service.
- Fake reviews, fake profiles, and multiple accounts for the same person.

4. Profiles and photos
- Use recent photos of yourself. No swimsuit, lingerie or suggestive photos.
- Describe what you actually offer, at the rate you actually charge.
- No phone numbers, social handles or payment details in your public Phriend profile. Share them in the chat instead.

5. Teams
A team is a few ID-verified Phriends who offer a service together, for example a guide, a photographer and a driver for one day out. Every member follows the same rules as on their own profile.
- The team lead is responsible for the team page: the members, roles, prices and payment terms must be real and accurate.
- One booking covers the members named on it. If anyone else turns up, do not proceed: leave and report, as on any booking.
- The downpayment, at most 50% and paid in cash, in person, goes to the team lead, and the team splits it among themselves. Phriend never holds the money.
- Either side can cancel as with any booking. If a member cannot make it, the team lead cancels or rebooks.

6. Zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive behaviour
Objectionable content and abusive behaviour are not tolerated on Phriend. Profiles, photos, gigs and chat messages pass an automated filter, and a person approves every Phriend profile before it goes live. Any member can report a profile, gig, review or message from the report button in the app, or by email to support@phriend.app, and can block another member instantly from the chat. We review every report within 24 hours, remove the offending content, and remove the account of any member who breaks these rules. There is no warning for the items in section 3.

7. Consequences
Breaking these guidelines leads to immediate removal of the account and any related accounts. Where the law requires it, or where someone's safety is at risk, we report to the authorities and cooperate fully with investigations.
There is no warning system for the prohibited items in section 3. Offensive language in chat is refused automatically: the first two attempts only warn, then the sender is muted for 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days in turn, and our moderators review every flag and can ban. For other lesser issues such as a late cancellation, we may warn first, then suspend, then remove.

8. Reporting
Use the report button on any profile or gig, or email support@phriend.app. Tell us the profile name and what happened. Reports are confidential. See the safety and transaction rules for what to do in an emergency.
